---
title: "Singular value decomposition"
---

One rank-one pattern leaves substantial structure in the centered [PHOIBLE matrix](rank-one-structure.qmd). The singular value decomposition (SVD) expresses that matrix as a sequence of mutually orthogonal rank-one terms, ordered by the centered sum of squares each term represents.

## Stating the reduced decomposition

For $\mathbf Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with rank $r$, the reduced SVD is

$$
\mathbf Z
=
\mathbf U\mathbf D\mathbf V^{\mathsf T},
$$

where

$$
\mathbf U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r},
\qquad
\mathbf D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r},
\qquad
\mathbf V\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}.
$$

The columns are orthonormal,

$$
\mathbf U^{\mathsf T}\mathbf U=\mathbf I_r,
\qquad
\mathbf V^{\mathsf T}\mathbf V=\mathbf I_r,
$$

and $\mathbf D$ is diagonal with ordered nonnegative entries,

$$
d_1\ge d_2\ge\cdots\ge d_r>0.
$$

The vectors $\mathbf u_k$ locate the row objects along component $k$, the vectors $\mathbf v_k$ define the corresponding column directions, and $d_k$ gives the component's strength.

## From a matrix product to rank-one terms

Multiplying by the diagonal matrix scales matched columns of $\mathbf U$ and $\mathbf V$. Thus

$$
\mathbf Z
=
\sum_{k=1}^{r}
d_k\mathbf u_k\mathbf v_k^{\mathsf T}.
$$

Every summand is rank one. The rank-$K$ approximation keeps the first $K$ terms:

$$
\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(K)}
=
\sum_{k=1}^{K}
d_k\mathbf u_k\mathbf v_k^{\mathsf T}
=
\mathbf U_K\mathbf D_K\mathbf V_K^{\mathsf T}.
$$

Among all rank-$K$ matrices, this approximation minimizes squared reconstruction error:

$$
\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(K)}
=
\arg\min_{\operatorname{rank}(\mathbf A)\le K}
\|\mathbf Z-\mathbf A\|_F^2.
$$

The Frobenius norm is the sum of squared cells,

$$
\|\mathbf A\|_F^2
=
\sum_i\sum_j a_{ij}^2.
$$

Orthogonality yields

$$
\|\mathbf Z\|_F^2
=
\sum_{k=1}^{r}d_k^2,
\qquad
\|\mathbf Z-\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(K)}\|_F^2
=
\sum_{k=K+1}^{r}d_k^2.
$$

Thus the singular values order components by their contribution to the observed centered matrix.

## Computing the PHOIBLE decomposition

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

phoible <- readRDS("data/phoible/phoible-pilot.rds")
inventories <- phoible$inventories[
  order(phoible$inventories$glottocode,
        as.integer(phoible$inventories$inventory_id)),
]
groups <- split(seq_len(nrow(inventories)), inventories$glottocode)
RNGkind(sample.kind = "Rejection")
set.seed(20260827L)
chosen <- vapply(groups, function(x) x[[sample.int(length(x), 1L)]], integer(1))
selected <- inventories[unname(chosen), ]

area <- selected$macroarea
area[is.na(area) | area == ""] <- "Unclassified"
selected$split <- NA_character_
set.seed(20261018L)
for (name in sort(unique(area))) {
  index <- sample(which(area == name))
  n_holdout <- floor(0.15 * length(index))
  selected$split[index[seq_len(n_holdout)]] <- "validation"
  selected$split[index[n_holdout + seq_len(n_holdout)]] <- "test"
  selected$split[index[is.na(selected$split[index])]] <- "training"
}
training_rows <- which(selected$split == "training")

memberships <- merge(
  phoible$memberships,
  selected[c("inventory_id", "glottocode")],
  by = c("inventory_id", "glottocode")
)
frequency <- table(
  memberships$segment_id[memberships$glottocode %in%
    selected$glottocode[training_rows]]
)
column_ids <- sort(names(frequency)[frequency >= 20L])
X <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = nrow(selected),
  ncol = length(column_ids),
  dimnames = list(selected$glottocode, column_ids)
)
retained <- memberships[memberships$segment_id %in% column_ids, ]
X[cbind(
  match(retained$glottocode, rownames(X)),
  match(retained$segment_id, colnames(X))
)] <- 1

training_mean <- colMeans(X[training_rows, , drop = FALSE])
Z <- sweep(X[training_rows, , drop = FALSE], 2, training_mean, "-")
decomposition <- svd(Z)

orthogonality_checks <- c(
  U = max(abs(crossprod(decomposition$u) - diag(ncol(decomposition$u)))),
  V = max(abs(crossprod(decomposition$v) - diag(ncol(decomposition$v))))
)
orthogonality_checks
```

The empirical training matrix is `r nrow(Z)` by `r ncol(Z)`. The largest absolute departures from the two orthogonality identities are `r format(max(orthogonality_checks), scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)` under this numerical fit.

## Reading the empirical spectrum

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4

spectrum <- data.frame(
  component = seq_along(decomposition$d),
  singular_value = decomposition$d,
  variance_fraction = decomposition$d^2 / sum(decomposition$d^2),
  cumulative_fraction = cumsum(decomposition$d^2) / sum(decomposition$d^2)
)

ggplot(spectrum[spectrum$component <= 64, ],
       aes(x = component, y = variance_fraction)) +
  geom_line(color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.65) +
  geom_point(color = "grey20", size = 1.2) + # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  labs(x = "Component", y = "Fraction of centered sum of squares") +
  theme_classic()
```

The first component accounts for `r scales::percent(spectrum$variance_fraction[[1]], accuracy = 0.1)` of centered sum of squares. The first forty account for `r scales::percent(spectrum$cumulative_fraction[[40]], accuracy = 0.1)`. These are descriptive properties of the training matrix. They do not select a predictive rank and do not turn the components into linguistic categories.

## Sign and directional limits

For any component,

$$
d_k\mathbf u_k\mathbf v_k^{\mathsf T}
=
d_k(-\mathbf u_k)(-\mathbf v_k)^{\mathsf T}.
$$

Software may thus reverse both signs without changing the fitted matrix. Interpretation should concern contrasts among loadings or scores, not a privileged positive orientation.

If singular values are equal or nearly equal, rotations within the corresponding subspace can also leave the fit unchanged or nearly unchanged. The subspace may then be more stable than any one plotted axis. This is a stronger limitation than sign indeterminacy.

## Checking the ordered patterns

1. What are the dimensions of $\mathbf U$, $\mathbf D$, and $\mathbf V$?
2. Why is each term $d_k\mathbf u_k\mathbf v_k^{\mathsf T}$ rank one?
3. Why do squared singular values add to centered sum of squares?
4. What does the scree plot summarize, and what does it not select?
5. Why may an SVD component reverse sign across software runs?

The [next page](principal-component-analysis.qmd) shows why the same right singular vectors are the principal-component directions of the centered PHOIBLE matrix.
